# Alpha.6 saved-answer inputs

Captured with Specify 0.1.0-alpha.6, quiddity/haecceity v0.1.0-alpha.8
(c62081c6), before changing the dependency pin. Each gzip contains the actual STEP
writer output, including the original schema-2 base64 payload and semantic PMI.
JSON companions retain the original features and all explicitly accepted answers.
These are immutable compatibility inputs, not regenerated expectations.

Inputs: plate, GRM-02_shaft, four_corner_holes_are_quiddity_rectangle_with_members,
and pin from ../parts. plate-moved rotates every Cartesian point and direction of
plate by Ry(23 degrees) Rx(37 degrees), then translates points by (31,-17,43) mm,
before analysis and writing with the alpha.6 build. Its JSON records that motion.

Every question default was explicitly accepted to the fixed point; material and a
Unicode/quoted/backslash note were supplied. Reopening must preserve that literal
text and must either migrate each feature answer or explain why it remains open.

CTC-02 RC and FTC-10 RB were captured separately from the exact Specify
`v0.1.0-alpha.6` tag (f045e4e), quiddity/haecceity alpha.8 c62081c6.
The sandbox refused creation of a `.git` file in the requested sibling worktree;
the writer was built from a pristine `git archive` of that tag there instead.
`ctc02-reid` contains 34 accepted answers; reopening under 0.1.1 reports the two
missing linear-pattern answers, retaining 32. `ftc10-reid` contains 29 accepted
answers; two use the old linear-pattern ID with eight bore faces, whose support
grows to twelve faces. Reopening carries both to the unique same-kind superset.
Its two newly recognised-pattern questions stay open. The fixtures were committed
in separate capture-only commits before their new-kernel tests were written.
